The appellant was a lessee of a certain land in the State of Bombay. The appellant was a tenant of the land in dispute. The appellant filed a suit for a declaration that the land was not a public purpose within the meaning of section 2(b) of the Bombay Land Revenue Act, 1953, and the appellant was entitled to the benefit of the provisions of section 2 (b) of that Act. The trial court decreed the suit. The appellant appealed to the High Court. The High Court held that the land in question was a public purpose and that the appellant was not a lessee of the land. The High court held that the appellant had no right to the benefit under section 2 (d) of the Act. The High. Court held that section 2 (c) of the Madras Land Revenue Act was not applicable to the facts of the present case. The appellant 's appeal to the High court was dismissed. In appeal to this Court, HELD : (i) The High Court was right in holding that the appellant 's right to the benefits under section 2(d) of that section was not a right to the advantage of the appellant.
